_about: Small cruiser (Track SH, the warship, 2026-10-10). ALEX'S (decision mixed-warfare): 'You have a huge ship parked off the coast but you need tanks to move inland to spot the aa batteries for the ship', and the warship is 'not a full battleship, something smaller that would operate more independently'; its main guns are a special, 'fired by hand with a long reload, aimed with the target selection', and a long-range gun needs a SPOTTED target (shared spotting: 'Yes'); the unit sheet's small cruiser is his choice 'as proposed' (decision unit-sheet-choices; reference/mockups/unit_sheet.html genCruiser: 112 to 128 m, turrets fore and aft, its accent on the quarterdeck panel); the boats are drawn at the planes' scale (decision water-layer) with an ink V wake (decision boat-wake). EVERYTHING ELSE HERE IS PROPOSED by Track SH. The planes' movement system with a heavy ship's numbers, as the patrol boat's (data/units/patrol_boat.json) with more of everything: on the surface band, a slow turn that needs way on, a speed of 12 m/s cruise and 15 m/s flat out (about 23 and 29 knots) against the cutter's 10 and 15 and a fighter's 100: a ship covers 30 m in a 2.5 s step and 60 m in a turn, a kilometre in 17 turns. Its turn is wide: a rudder needs flow and a 120 m hull needs room, 191 m radius at cruise (1.6 hull lengths, a circle of 100 s, twenty turns). The WATER RULE (World.set_water, data/sim/sea.json) keeps it on water at least draught_m deep, at its centre and at both ends of its hull (60 m fore and aft), so it keeps out of the shallows (0 to 6 m, data/world/water.json) by its own length: the centre about 160 m off a straight coast. Its guns: auto-firing FLAK, weapon ship_flak (ALEX, decision weapon-kinds, 2026-10-11: 'Flak would be shells shot that then explode. ... Flak is pointed up and machine guns are around and less up. So flak guns have better coverage in the area directly above them.'; on the mapping 'the cruiser's AA is flak': '5 good'). It was the id aa_guns, shared with the cutter and the mobile AA; those two are machine guns now (quad_mg, deck_mg) and this one keeps the upward cone: the battery's light flak on four mounts (two abeam of the bridge, two aft), all around, aimed up from 2 degrees above the horizon to straight overhead, so it is the one AA weapon on the water that covers the plane straight over the ship; short (320 m, so they reach the low band over the ship and never the medium band). It draws flak BURSTS (F2, like the battery's), not tracers: it is not in data/fx/fx.json tracers.weapons. Every number is the former aa_guns' own (PROPOSED, unchanged on purpose); and ONE special, 'main_guns' (Main Guns Fire): data/sim/guns.json says what it does. One special makes it a single unit, not a nest. It carries no bombs. At 0 health it is DESTROYED (fate 'destroyed': it stays where it was, down; the drawing may sink it).
name: Small cruiser

size_m._reason: the unit sheet's small cruiser: genCruiser draws a length of 112 to 128 m; 120 is the middle, the length it is drawn at and the hull the water rule checks

draught_m._reason: a light cruiser draws 5 to 6.5 m. 6 m is exactly the top of the generator's shallows step (0 to 6 m; data/world/water.json depth steps): the ship keeps to the shelf and the deep, never the shallows, and with its 60 m of hull each side of the centre it stays 160 m or so off a straight coast

actions_per_turn._reason: a slow unit plans two points a turn (2.5 s steps, data/sim/turn.json), as the boats: a step is 30 m at cruise, a quarter of its own length

health._reason: the hardest unit to sink: more than the bomber (8) and the radio tower (8), with the bridge (10) near it. A bomb's direct hit is 3 pips (data/sim/bombs.json) and a bomber has three drops of four bombs: one pass of a full stick leaves a hole in it, not a wreck. Light fighters' guns do 1 a hit

sight_range_m._reason: a LONG sight, as a bridge twenty metres up has: over a fighter's 800 m and a patrol boat's 450 m. Spotters on land still matter: the guns reach 3 km (data/sim/guns.json)

material._reason: PROPOSED by builder G3 (2026-10-12; the board's table, variants/gunfire/board.json material_table, which Alex's decisions damage-looks, 'the model makes sense', and gunfire-looks, G3, put to use): a steel hull. Decides what a round that lands on it does (data/fx/fx.json gunfire): metal.

enabled._reason: a ship smokes when hit; a SUNK ship draws no damage (decision ship-sinks)

source_m._reason: a funnel's smoke: the top of Alex's 'about 8 m', not the 120 m hull (the puff was 41 to 96 m in radius)

source_back_m._reason: the funnels stand abaft amidships: 12 m behind the centre of a 120 m hull

rise_mps._reason: the smoulder's rate: a damaged ground or sea unit smokes like a ruin or a wreck (data/fx/fx.json ruin R1 and crash A smolder rise_mps 4.0), so its puffs climb into the faster air above and the plume leans downwind (decisions smoke-consistency, wind-with-height). PROPOSED

shape._about: One box: the hull and superstructure averaged (a ship is one box, Alex's two layers are for ground vehicles). Every number PROPOSED.

stamp._reason: a target, not scenery: other lines are not blocked by it

length_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): 120 m, the unit's size_m

width_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): 15 m, a small cruiser's beam

bottom_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): from the water's surface (the draught is below it and does not count)

top_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): 10 m, a main deck 5 m up and a superstructure over it, averaged

speed_min_mps._reason: slow astern: a ship can reverse once stopped (design doc, Motion and inertia: ships can reverse once stopped), which is also how it backs off a shore the water rule has held it at

speed_cruise_mps._reason: about 23 knots: a cruiser's steady speed, scaled to the 5 km map like the cutter's 10 m/s (a heavy ship is not faster than a launch in a game where a plane crosses a map in eight turns)

speed_max_mps._reason: about 29 knots: flat out (the lead's brief: about 15 m/s)

dive_speed_max_mps._reason: a ship cannot dive: equal to speed_max_mps

accel_mps2._reason: from a stop to cruise in twenty seconds (four steps, two turns): a heavy hull, half the cutter's 1.2

decel_mps2._reason: water drag and the engines astern: a ship stops from cruise in twelve seconds, quicker than it gets going

reverse_from_stop._reason: design doc, Motion and inertia: ships can reverse once stopped; speed cannot cross zero within a step

turn_rate_curve_dps._reason: a rudder needs flow (data/units/_schema.json): no turn with no way on, 3.6 deg/s at cruise, a little less flat out. At cruise that is a turn radius of 191 m (1.6 hull lengths) and a full circle in 100 s, twenty turns: a wide turn beside the cutter's 57 m radius and a fighter's 286 m at ten times the speed. A step can turn it 9 degrees

turn_bleed_mps2._reason: a ship loses little way in a turn (a heavy hull): at the full rate 0.3 m/s per second, 0.75 m/s over a step

turn_bleed_exponent._reason: as the planes' (induced drag): gentle turns are nearly free

altitude_bands._reason: it rides the sea: the surface band (data/sim/altitude.json). The bombs reach it (they hurt a unit at the surface)

round._reason: ALEX (decision weapon-kinds, 2026-10-11): the cruiser's AA is flak ('5 good'): 'Flak would be shells shot that then explode.' PROPOSED by builder G3: a SMALL flak shell, the same 320 m reach as the battery's light flak (the board's mapping did not name ship_flak); a burst in the air (F2)

hardpoints._reason: four gun mounts: two to port and starboard abeam of the bridge (22 m forward of the middle, 5 m out, 6 m above the water) and two aft (26 m abaft the middle). Each mount rolls on its own

mount_deg._reason: the cone is all around (half_across_deg 180), so the mount does not matter; 0 is the bow

half_across_deg._reason: all around, as the battery's flak: the guns fire at anything above them whichever way the ship points

elevation_deg._reason: the battery's flak cone, so the ship and the battery agree on what is above them: centred 46 degrees above the horizon. KEPT by decision weapon-kinds (Alex: 'Flak is pointed up ... flak guns have better coverage in the area directly above them'): flak is the upward cone

half_height_deg._reason: from 2 degrees above the horizon to straight up, as the battery's flak: nothing is out of the cone for being low, and a plane straight over the ship is in it (the machine guns' cones, the horizon to 50 degrees, do not reach it). KEPT by decision weapon-kinds. The odds stay flat across the cone (rim_odds_factor 1), so 'better coverage directly above' is coverage, not a higher chance there: a peak overhead would be elevation 90, half 88 and a rim factor under 1, one data edit and not decided

effective_range_m._reason: the battery's LIGHT flak and the cutter's: short, so it covers the low band (120 m) round the ship and not the medium band (400 m). A plane at medium is never touched by a cruiser's light guns

base_hit_chance._reason: the battery's light flak's own per-roll chance, unchanged by decision weapon-kinds. MEASURED 2026-10-11 (builder AA, tmp/aa/aa_probe.gd): expected pips per pass of a bomber at cruise in the low band, straight over the ship / 300 m aside, 3.94 / 1.74 (a light fighter 3.25 / 1.45), the same before and after the split; the medium band 0

rim_odds_factor._reason: flat, as every flexible gun: a gun crew aims within the arc

falloff_exponent._reason: no effect while the factor is flat (rim_odds_factor 1)

tracking_dps._reason: the battery's light flak: fast tracking, a light gun

damage_pips._reason: one pip a hit like every other gun

rolls_per_second._reason: the cutter's: two a second on each of FOUR mounts, so the cruiser puts out twice the cutter's volume (0.56 hits a second on a plane in range before the other factors), the battery's light flak's 0.28 doubled

traverse_dps._reason: PROPOSED by builder ORD (2026-10-14; Alex, decision tank-fire-feedback: 'The turret feedback should also apply to the ship'): the main turrets turn together at 10 degrees a second (the lead's example; a heavy turret is slower than a tank's 25), so 90 degrees takes 9 s, nearly two turns, and the salvo leaves when they are on bearing. A scenario trains them on the first target at the start (add_unit's turret_deg); an order whose turrets cannot come round within the turn turns them as far as it can and fires next turn

half_arc_deg._reason: all round: the cruiser has turrets fore and aft and trains either end, so the guns bear on any side (the turrets take the short way to a bearing). A narrower arc would be a blind sector; nothing in the design doc asks for one

barrel_tip_m._reason: from a turret's axis to its barrels' tips along the bearing: the drawn gun house's front (turret_r 3.4 to 4.2 x 0.85) and the barrel (8.5 to 11.5 m), 13.46 m on the game's own cruiser model (the scene seed's generated small cruiser; the muzzle smoke itself takes the DRAWN barrels, UnitMarkerArt.ship_muzzles, so this number is the data's statement of it and a test holds the two near each other).
